title: GitHub Actions with OIDC federation: deploying without a stored secret

videos.script: A pipeline that deploys to Azure has to prove who it is. {{who}} The old way is a password. A client secret, pasted into the repository's settings. It lasts a year or two, and every copy of it is the identity. {{secret}} The new way stores nothing. GitHub signs a short token for one run of one workflow. Azure has been told, in advance, which tokens to trust. {{trust}} The whole security of it is one line: the subject. Which repository, which branch, which environment. {{subject}} By the end of this lesson, you can write that trust, read a subject, and say who could deploy with it. {{end}}
